# Purpose
This document stores the code used to create datasets for the GEO 330 final group projects, along with descriptions of each dataset and suggestions for how it may inform a group's analyses. Datasets are added iteratively, one group at a time:

| Group | Topic | Datasets |
|-------|-------|----------|
| 1 | E-bike safety and legislation in the city of Chicago | Bicycle crashes (points); bicycle crashes by community area and year (polygons) |
| 2 | Bus rapid transit (BRT) along Ashland Avenue | Ashland and connecting bus routes (lines) and nearby rail stations (points) with current and pre-pandemic ridership; Ashland bus stops (points); CTA rail lines; monthly bus and rail ridership |
| 3 | Pedestrian safety near CTA rail stations | Pedestrian crashes (points); CTA rail stations with pedestrian crash counts within 25, 50 and 100 feet (points and buffers) |
| 4 | Motorcycle fatalities in the city of Chicago | Fatal motorcycle crashes (points); motorcycle fatalities citywide and by community area and year |

Each dataset is saved to `projects/data/` as a GeoPackage (spatial layers), CSV files (tables, for Excel or Tableau) and an `.RData` file (for R and Posit Cloud). Each download is also saved as a cache file in the data directory, which is read instead when the source cannot be reached.

# Settings
```{r}
#| label: settings

data_dir <- "projects/data"

# create the data directory if needed (git does not track empty directories)
dir.create(data_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Chicago Data Portal (Socrata) datasets
portal_resource <- "https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/%s.csv"
id_crashes <- "85ca-t3if" # Traffic Crashes - Crashes
id_people <- "u6pd-qa9d"  # Traffic Crashes - People
url_community_areas <- "https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/igwz-8jzy.geojson"

# Chicago Health Atlas community area population (same as Exercise #3)
url_health_atlas <- "https://chicagohealthatlas.org/api/v1/data/?format=json&layer=neighborhood&population=&period=%s&topic=%s"
population_period <- "2020-2024"

# maximum number of rows returned by a single portal request
soql_limit <- 1000000
```

# Functions for data development
```{r}
#| label: data development functions

# download a file to its cache path; if the download fails, the existing cache
# file (from an earlier run) is used instead. The download goes to a temporary
# file first so a failed download does not overwrite the cache.
download_cached <- function(url, cache) {
  dir.create(dirname(cache), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = paste0(".", tools::file_ext(cache)))
  ok <- tryCatch({
    download.file(url, tmp, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
    file.exists(tmp) && file.size(tmp) > 0 && file.copy(tmp, cache, overwrite = TRUE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Download failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    FALSE
  })
  if (!ok) {
    if (!file.exists(cache)) stop("Download failed and no cache file found: ", cache)
    message("Download failed; using cache file ", cache)
  }
  cache
}

# Chicago Data Portal request (SoQL) URL for a dataset id, e.g.
# soql_url(id_crashes, `$where` = "first_crash_type = 'PEDALCYCLIST'")
soql_url <- function(id, ...) {
  params <- list(...)
  values <- map_chr(params, ~ URLencode(format(.x, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE), reserved = TRUE))
  paste0(sprintf(portal_resource, id), "?", paste0(names(params), "=", values, collapse = "&"))
}

# portal CSV read as text; columns are converted where they are used
read_portal_csv <- function(url, cache) {
  read_csv(download_cached(url, cache), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
}

read_portal_geojson <- function(url, cache) {
  st_read(download_cached(url, cache), quiet = TRUE)
}

# save a group's datasets (object names) to an .RData file, along with the
# community area boundaries in WGS84 (epsg:4326)
save_with_community_areas <- function(objects, file) {
  caller <- parent.frame()
  env <- new.env()
  for (obj in objects) assign(obj, get(obj, envir = caller), envir = env)
  env$community_areas <- st_transform(community_areas, 4326)
  save(list = c(objects, "community_areas"), envir = env, file = file)
}

# portal records for a long list of ids, requested in batches (to keep URLs short)
# and combined into a single cache file
read_portal_ids <- function(id, field, ids, cache, batch_size = 40) {
  if (length(ids) == 0) return(tibble())
  batches <- split(ids, ceiling(seq_along(ids) / batch_size))
  result <- tryCatch({
    map(batches, function(batch) {
      where <- sprintf("%s in (%s)", field, paste0("'", batch, "'", collapse = ","))
      read_csv(soql_url(id, `$where` = where, `$limit` = soql_limit),
               col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
    }) %>%
      bind_rows()
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Download failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })
  if (is.null(result)) {
    if (!file.exists(cache)) stop("Download failed and no cache file found: ", cache)
    message("Download failed; using cache file ", cache)
    return(read_csv(cache, col_types = cols(.default = col_character())))
  }
  write_csv(result, cache)
  result
}
```

# Shared geographic data
## Community areas
Community area boundaries (N=77) are downloaded from the [Chicago Data Portal](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Facilities-Geographic-Boundaries/Boundaries-Community-Areas/igwz-8jzy/about_data) and projected to Illinois State Plane East (epsg:3435, US feet) for spatial analysis. Population (2020-2024 American Community Survey estimates) comes from the [Chicago Health Atlas](https://chicagohealthatlas.org) and is used to calculate rates.

```{r}
#| label: community areas

community_areas <- read_portal_geojson(url_community_areas,
                                       file.path(data_dir, "community_areas_cache.geojson")) %>%
  st_transform(3435) %>%
  mutate(comarea_id = as.numeric(area_numbe),
         comarea_name = str_to_title(community),
         area_sqmi = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 27878400) %>% # square feet to square miles
  select(comarea_id, comarea_name, area_sqmi) %>%
  arrange(comarea_id)

community_areas_population <- fromJSON(download_cached(
  sprintf(url_health_atlas, population_period, "POP"),
  file.path(data_dir, "health_atlas_population_cache.json")))$results %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  filter(str_starts(g, "1714000-")) %>% # Chicago community areas (results include other cities)
  transmute(comarea_id = as.numeric(str_replace(g, "1714000-", "")),
            population = as.numeric(v)) %>%
  drop_na(comarea_id)

community_areas <- community_areas %>%
  left_join(community_areas_population, by = "comarea_id")
```

# Group 1: E-bike safety and legislation in the city of Chicago
## Project overview
Group 1 is examining how e-bike legislation relates to bicyclist injuries, and which other factors (e.g., bike infrastructure and street connectivity) might influence those outcomes. The datasets below describe where, when and under what conditions bicycle crashes occurred in Chicago over the past five full calendar years, and how crash counts, severe injuries and rates differ among community areas and change over time.

## Settings
```{r}
#| label: group 1 settings

# five full calendar years of crashes (update each year)
g1_years <- 2021:2025

# crash dates are local (Chicago) time
g1_where_dates <- sprintf("crash_date >= '%d-01-01T00:00:00' AND crash_date < '%d-01-01T00:00:00'",
                          min(g1_years), max(g1_years) + 1)

# crashes farther than this distance (feet) from a community area are left unassigned
g1_snap_ft <- 500

# bicyclist injury classifications, least to most severe
injury_levels <- c("NO INDICATION OF INJURY", "REPORTED, NOT EVIDENT",
                   "NONINCAPACITATING INJURY", "INCAPACITATING INJURY", "FATAL")

# output files
g1_gpkg <- file.path(data_dir, "group01_bike_crashes.gpkg")
g1_rdata <- file.path(data_dir, "group01_bike_crashes.RData")
```

## Data sources
Crash records come from two related Chicago Data Portal datasets, joined by `crash_record_id`:

- [Traffic Crashes - Crashes](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Transportation/Traffic-Crashes-Crashes/85ca-t3if/about_data): one record per crash on city streets within the city of Chicago, reported by the Chicago Police Department (CPD), with the crash's location, conditions, contributing causes and crash-level injury totals.
- [Traffic Crashes - People](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Transportation/Traffic-Crashes-People/u6pd-qa9d/about_data): one record per person involved in a crash (drivers, passengers, pedestrians and bicyclists), with each person's injury classification, age and sex.

A crash is identified as a **bicycle crash** when its first crash type is `PEDALCYCLIST` (Crashes dataset) *or* at least one person involved was a bicyclist (`person_type = 'BICYCLE'`, People dataset). Using both captures crashes in which a bicyclist was involved but the first harmful event was something else (e.g., a vehicle that struck a parked car and then a bicyclist).

## Download bicycle crash records
```{r}
#| label: group 1 download crash records

# bicyclists involved in crashes
g1_people <- read_portal_csv(
  soql_url(id_people,
           `$where` = paste(g1_where_dates, "AND person_type = 'BICYCLE'"),
           `$limit` = soql_limit),
  file.path(data_dir, "group01_people_bicycle_cache.csv"))

# crashes with a first crash type of PEDALCYCLIST
g1_crashes_pedalcyclist <- read_portal_csv(
  soql_url(id_crashes,
           `$where` = paste(g1_where_dates, "AND first_crash_type = 'PEDALCYCLIST'"),
           `$limit` = soql_limit),
  file.path(data_dir, "group01_crashes_pedalcyclist_cache.csv"))

# other crashes involving a bicyclist
g1_crashes_other <- read_portal_ids(
  id_crashes, "crash_record_id",
  setdiff(unique(g1_people$crash_record_id), g1_crashes_pedalcyclist$crash_record_id),
  file.path(data_dir, "group01_crashes_other_cache.csv"))

g1_crashes_raw <- bind_rows(g1_crashes_pedalcyclist, g1_crashes_other) %>%
  distinct(crash_record_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

## Bicyclists by crash
Bicyclist records are summarized by crash: the number of bicyclists involved, the number killed and seriously (incapacitating) injured, and the injury classification, age, sex, action, visibility and location of the most severely injured bicyclist. Bicyclist injuries are more useful than the crash-level injury columns for a bicycle safety analysis, because the crash-level columns also count injuries to drivers and passengers.

```{r}
#| label: group 1 bicyclists by crash

g1_cyclists <- g1_people %>%
  mutate(injury = factor(injury_classification, levels = injury_levels, ordered = TRUE),
         age = as.numeric(age),
         age = if_else(age <= 0 | age > 110, NA_real_, age)) %>% # implausible ages
  arrange(crash_record_id, desc(injury)) %>%
  group_by(crash_record_id) %>%
  summarise(n_cyclists = n(),
            n_cyclists_killed = sum(injury == "FATAL", na.rm = TRUE),
            n_cyclists_seriously_injured = sum(injury == "INCAPACITATING INJURY", na.rm = TRUE),
            n_cyclists_injured = sum(injury >= "NONINCAPACITATING INJURY", na.rm = TRUE),
            cyclist_injury = as.character(first(injury)),
            cyclist_age = first(age),
            cyclist_sex = first(sex),
            cyclist_action = first(pedpedal_action),
            cyclist_visibility = first(pedpedal_visibility),
            cyclist_location = first(pedpedal_location),
            .groups = "drop")
```

## Bicycle crash points
Crashes are located with their latitude and longitude, and attributed with the community area they fall within. Crashes with missing coordinates are dropped, and crashes just outside a community area boundary (e.g., on a bridge or along the lakefront) are assigned to the nearest community area within `g1_snap_ft` feet.

```{r}
#| label: group 1 bicycle crash points

g1_crashes <- g1_crashes_raw %>%
  mutate(bike_source = case_when(
    first_crash_type == "PEDALCYCLIST" & crash_record_id %in% g1_people$crash_record_id ~ "both",
    first_crash_type == "PEDALCYCLIST" ~ "first crash type",
    TRUE ~ "bicyclist record")) %>%
  select(crash_record_id, crash_date, posted_speed_limit, traffic_control_device,
         weather_condition, lighting_condition, first_crash_type, trafficway_type,
         roadway_surface_cond, crash_type, intersection_related_i, hit_and_run_i,
         dooring_i, prim_contributory_cause, sec_contributory_cause, street_no,
         street_direction, street_name, num_units, damage, most_severe_injury,
         injuries_total, injuries_fatal, injuries_incapacitating, latitude, longitude,
         bike_source) %>%
  mutate(crash_date = ymd_hms(crash_date, tz = "America/Chicago", truncated = 3),
         crash_year = year(crash_date),
         crash_month = month(crash_date),
         crash_hour = hour(crash_date),
         crash_day_of_week = wday(crash_date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
         across(c(posted_speed_limit, num_units, injuries_total, injuries_fatal,
                  injuries_incapacitating, latitude, longitude), as.numeric),
         across(c(intersection_related_i, hit_and_run_i, dooring_i), ~ replace_na(.x, "N")),
         ksi_crash = injuries_fatal + injuries_incapacitating > 0) %>%
  left_join(g1_cyclists, by = "crash_record_id") %>%
  mutate(n_cyclists = replace_na(n_cyclists, 0),
         across(c(n_cyclists_killed, n_cyclists_seriously_injured, n_cyclists_injured),
                ~ replace_na(.x, 0))) %>%
  filter(crash_year %in% g1_years) %>%
  arrange(crash_date)

# crashes without usable coordinates (reported in the checks below)
g1_crashes_unlocated <- g1_crashes %>%
  filter(is.na(latitude) | is.na(longitude) | latitude == 0 | longitude == 0)

bike_crashes <- g1_crashes %>%
  anti_join(g1_crashes_unlocated, by = "crash_record_id") %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) %>%
  st_transform(3435)

# nearest community area and distance (0 for crashes within a community area)
nearest_ca <- st_nearest_feature(bike_crashes, community_areas)
nearest_ft <- as.numeric(st_distance(bike_crashes, community_areas[nearest_ca, ], by_element = TRUE))

bike_crashes <- bike_crashes %>%
  mutate(comarea_id = if_else(nearest_ft <= g1_snap_ft,
                              community_areas$comarea_id[nearest_ca], NA_real_)) %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(community_areas) %>% select(comarea_id, comarea_name),
            by = "comarea_id") %>%
  relocate(comarea_id, comarea_name, .before = bike_source)

rm(nearest_ca, nearest_ft)
```

## Bicycle crashes by community area and year
Crashes are counted by community area and year. Every community area appears in every year (N = 77 x 5 = 385 rows), with zeros where no crashes occurred. Rates use the community area's 2020-2024 population and land area, so changes between years reflect changes in crashes, not population.

```{r}
#| label: group 1 crashes by community area and year

g1_count_cols <- c("crashes", "crashes_injury", "crashes_ksi", "crashes_dooring",
                   "crashes_hit_and_run", "cyclists_injured", "cyclists_seriously_injured",
                   "cyclists_killed")

bike_crashes_ca_year_table <- bike_crashes %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.na(comarea_id)) %>%
  group_by(comarea_id, crash_year) %>%
  summarise(crashes = n(),
            crashes_injury = sum(injuries_total > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            crashes_ksi = sum(ksi_crash, na.rm = TRUE),
            crashes_dooring = sum(dooring_i == "Y"),
            crashes_hit_and_run = sum(hit_and_run_i == "Y"),
            cyclists_injured = sum(n_cyclists_injured),
            cyclists_seriously_injured = sum(n_cyclists_seriously_injured),
            cyclists_killed = sum(n_cyclists_killed),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(comarea_id = community_areas$comarea_id, crash_year = g1_years) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(g1_count_cols), ~ replace_na(.x, 0L))) %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(community_areas), by = "comarea_id") %>%
  mutate(crashes_per_10k = round(crashes / population * 10000, 2),
         crashes_per_sqmi = round(crashes / area_sqmi, 2),
         area_sqmi = round(area_sqmi, 2)) %>%
  select(comarea_id, comarea_name, crash_year, all_of(g1_count_cols),
         crashes_per_10k, crashes_per_sqmi, population, area_sqmi) %>%
  arrange(comarea_id, crash_year)

# long format (one row per community area and year) with community area boundaries
bike_crashes_ca_year <- community_areas %>%
  select(comarea_id) %>%
  right_join(bike_crashes_ca_year_table, by = "comarea_id") %>%
  arrange(comarea_id, crash_year)

# wide format (one row per community area) for mapping: crashes by year, total
# crashes, and change between the first and last year
bike_crashes_ca_wide <- community_areas %>%
  select(comarea_id, comarea_name, population, area_sqmi) %>%
  left_join(bike_crashes_ca_year_table %>%
              select(comarea_id, crash_year, crashes) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = crash_year, values_from = crashes,
                          names_prefix = "crashes_"),
            by = "comarea_id") %>%
  left_join(bike_crashes_ca_year_table %>%
              group_by(comarea_id) %>%
              summarise(crashes_total = sum(crashes),
                        crashes_ksi_total = sum(crashes_ksi),
                        cyclists_killed_total = sum(cyclists_killed)),
            by = "comarea_id") %>%
  mutate(crashes_change = .data[[paste0("crashes_", max(g1_years))]] -
           .data[[paste0("crashes_", min(g1_years))]],
         crashes_total_per_10k = round(crashes_total / population * 10000, 2),
         area_sqmi = round(area_sqmi, 2)) %>%
  arrange(comarea_id)

# city-wide totals by year (includes crashes not assigned to a community area)
bike_crashes_city_year <- bike_crashes %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  bind_rows(g1_crashes_unlocated) %>%
  group_by(crash_year) %>%
  summarise(crashes = n(),
            crashes_injury = sum(injuries_total > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            crashes_ksi = sum(ksi_crash, na.rm = TRUE),
            crashes_dooring = sum(dooring_i == "Y"),
            crashes_hit_and_run = sum(hit_and_run_i == "Y"),
            cyclists_injured = sum(n_cyclists_injured),
            cyclists_seriously_injured = sum(n_cyclists_seriously_injured),
            cyclists_killed = sum(n_cyclists_killed),
            .groups = "drop")
```

## Checks
```{r}
#| label: group 1 checks

# crashes by identification source (first crash type, bicyclist record or both)
count(g1_crashes, bike_source)

# crashes without coordinates and crashes not assigned to a community area
nrow(g1_crashes_unlocated)
sum(is.na(bike_crashes$comarea_id))

# city-wide totals by year
bike_crashes_city_year

# community area totals should equal assigned crashes
sum(bike_crashes_ca_year$crashes) == sum(!is.na(bike_crashes$comarea_id))

# total crashes by community area
ggplot(bike_crashes_ca_wide) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = crashes_total), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Crashes", direction = -1) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Bicycle crashes by community area, %d-%d", min(g1_years), max(g1_years))) +
  theme_void()
```

## Save datasets
Spatial layers are transformed to and saved in WGS84 (epsg:4326) so they can be used directly in web maps, Tableau and ArcGIS Online; transform them to Illinois State Plane East (epsg:3435) for distance and area calculations. The `.RData` file also includes the community area boundaries.

```{r}
#| label: group 1 save datasets

bike_crashes <- st_transform(bike_crashes, 4326)
bike_crashes_ca_year <- st_transform(bike_crashes_ca_year, 4326)
bike_crashes_ca_wide <- st_transform(bike_crashes_ca_wide, 4326)

# GeoPackage (one layer per dataset)
if (file.exists(g1_gpkg)) file.remove(g1_gpkg)
st_write(bike_crashes, g1_gpkg, layer = "bike_crashes", quiet = TRUE)
st_write(bike_crashes_ca_year, g1_gpkg, layer = "bike_crashes_ca_year", quiet = TRUE)
st_write(bike_crashes_ca_wide, g1_gpkg, layer = "bike_crashes_ca_wide", quiet = TRUE)

# CSV tables (points include latitude and longitude)
write_csv(st_drop_geometry(bike_crashes), file.path(data_dir, "group01_bike_crashes.csv"))
write_csv(bike_crashes_ca_year_table, file.path(data_dir, "group01_bike_crashes_ca_year.csv"))
write_csv(st_drop_geometry(bike_crashes_ca_wide), file.path(data_dir, "group01_bike_crashes_ca_wide.csv"))
write_csv(bike_crashes_city_year, file.path(data_dir, "group01_bike_crashes_city_year.csv"))

# R datasets
# (community areas are saved in WGS84 without changing the shared community_areas
# object, which later groups use in State Plane)
save_with_community_areas(c("bike_crashes", "bike_crashes_ca_year", "bike_crashes_ca_wide",
                            "bike_crashes_ca_year_table", "bike_crashes_city_year", "g1_years"),
                          g1_rdata)
```

## Dataset descriptions
### `bike_crashes` (points, one row per crash)
Bicycle crashes reported by CPD on city streets, `r min(g1_years)`-`r max(g1_years)`.

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `crash_record_id` | Unique crash id; links to the portal's Crashes, People and Vehicles datasets |
| `crash_date`, `crash_year`, `crash_month`, `crash_hour`, `crash_day_of_week` | Date and time of the crash (Chicago local time) |
| `posted_speed_limit` | Posted speed limit (mph) where the crash occurred |
| `traffic_control_device`, `trafficway_type`, `intersection_related_i` | Street design and control: signal or stop sign, street type (e.g., divided, one-way), and whether the crash was intersection related (Y/N) |
| `weather_condition`, `lighting_condition`, `roadway_surface_cond` | Conditions at the time of the crash |
| `first_crash_type` | First harmful event (e.g., `PEDALCYCLIST`, `TURNING`, `ANGLE`) |
| `crash_type` | Whether anyone was injured and/or a vehicle was towed |
| `dooring_i`, `hit_and_run_i` | Bicyclist struck by an opening vehicle door; driver left the scene (Y/N) |
| `prim_contributory_cause`, `sec_contributory_cause` | Primary and secondary causes, as judged by the responding officer |
| `street_no`, `street_direction`, `street_name` | Approximate street address |
| `num_units`, `damage` | Number of units (vehicles, bicycles) involved; estimated property damage |
| `most_severe_injury`, `injuries_total`, `injuries_fatal`, `injuries_incapacitating` | Crash-level injuries (all people involved, including drivers and passengers) |
| `ksi_crash` | Crash in which someone was killed or seriously (incapacitating) injured (TRUE/FALSE) |
| `n_cyclists`, `n_cyclists_injured`, `n_cyclists_seriously_injured`, `n_cyclists_killed` | Bicyclists involved, and bicyclists injured (non-incapacitating or worse), seriously injured and killed |
| `cyclist_injury`, `cyclist_age`, `cyclist_sex` | Injury classification, age and sex of the most severely injured bicyclist |
| `cyclist_action`, `cyclist_visibility`, `cyclist_location` | What the bicyclist was doing (e.g., riding with or against traffic), whether they had lights or reflective gear, and where they were (e.g., bike lane, crosswalk) |
| `latitude`, `longitude` | Crash location (WGS84) |
| `comarea_id`, `comarea_name` | Community area number and name |
| `bike_source` | How the crash was identified as a bicycle crash: `first crash type`, `bicyclist record` or `both` |

### `bike_crashes_ca_year` (polygons, one row per community area and year)
| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `comarea_id`, `comarea_name`, `crash_year` | Community area and year |
| `crashes` | Bicycle crashes |
| `crashes_injury`, `crashes_ksi` | Crashes with any injury; crashes with someone killed or seriously injured |
| `crashes_dooring`, `crashes_hit_and_run` | Dooring and hit-and-run crashes |
| `cyclists_injured`, `cyclists_seriously_injured`, `cyclists_killed` | Bicyclists injured, seriously injured and killed |
| `crashes_per_10k`, `crashes_per_sqmi` | Crashes per 10,000 residents and per square mile |
| `population`, `area_sqmi` | Population (2020-2024) and land area (square miles) |

`bike_crashes_ca_year_table` is the same table without boundaries (also saved as `group01_bike_crashes_ca_year.csv`). `bike_crashes_ca_wide` has one row per community area, with crashes by year in separate columns (`crashes_2021`, ..., `crashes_2025`), five-year totals, and the change in crashes between the first and last year. `bike_crashes_city_year` has city-wide totals by year.

## How these datasets may inform the project
- **Trends over time.** Plot `bike_crashes_city_year` to see whether bicycle crashes, serious injuries and deaths increased or decreased over the five years, and compare those trends with the timing of state and city e-bike legislation and policies the group identifies (e.g., Illinois' three-class e-bike law, Public Act 101-0444, effective January 1, 2020; Divvy's e-bike fleet expansion; city ordinances or enforcement changes). Monthly counts (`crash_month`) show seasonality, which matters when comparing periods before and after a policy change.
- **Where crashes occur.** Map `bike_crashes` (points or a heat map) and `bike_crashes_ca_wide` (choropleth of totals, rates or change) to identify hot spots and community areas where crashes are rising or falling. Compare counts with rates: community areas with many crashes (e.g., downtown and the North Side) also have the most bicycling, so rates per resident or square mile tell a different story than counts.
- **Severity and conditions.** Use `cyclist_injury`, `ksi_crash`, `posted_speed_limit`, `lighting_condition`, `crash_hour`, `first_crash_type`, `dooring_i` and `prim_contributory_cause` to ask which conditions are associated with more severe outcomes for bicyclists (e.g., higher speed limits, darkness, turning vehicles). Since faster e-bikes and higher-speed streets are central to e-bike regulation debates, the relationship between posted speed limit and injury severity is especially relevant.
- **Confounding factors.** The community area tables can be joined (by `comarea_id`) with other community-level data, such as bike lane miles from the portal's bike routes dataset, Divvy trips (Exercise #2; Divvy trip data distinguish `electric_bike` from `classic_bike` trips, which can serve as a rough measure of e-bike exposure), or Health Atlas indicators (Exercises #3 and #4), to account for differences in bicycling activity, infrastructure and demographics.
- **Comparisons with other cities.** These datasets cover Chicago only. They can be compared with similar open crash data from the other cities in the group's proposal (e.g., New York City's Motor Vehicle Collisions dataset, which codes e-bikes and e-scooters as vehicle types), using rates rather than counts.

## Limitations
- **E-bikes are not identified.** Chicago crash reports do not distinguish e-bikes from conventional bicycles, so these datasets describe all bicycle crashes. They provide context for e-bike safety (overall trends, where and under what conditions bicyclists are hurt), but cannot measure e-bike crashes directly.
- **Underreporting.** Only crashes reported to CPD are included. Crashes involving only bicyclists (e.g., falls, crashes between two bicyclists or with pedestrians), minor crashes and crashes reported later at police stations are underrepresented, and about half of all crash reports (mostly minor crashes) are self-reported by those involved at a police district rather than recorded at the scene by an officer.
- **Coverage.** Crashes on interstate highways and other roads patrolled by the Illinois State Police are not included. Crash records can be added or updated months after a crash, so counts for the most recent year may increase slightly when the data are recreated.
- **Counts are not exposure.** More crashes may simply reflect more bicycling. Rates per resident or square mile are a partial adjustment; bicycling activity (e.g., Divvy trips or bike counts) is a better denominator where available.

# Group 2: Bus rapid transit (BRT) along Ashland Avenue
## Project overview
Group 2 is studying BRT along Ashland Avenue. The datasets below describe current CTA ridership along the corridor: the Ashland bus routes (9 Ashland and X9 Ashland Express), the bus routes that cross or connect with them, and the CTA rail stations near them. Current ridership (the latest 12 months available) is compared with ridership in 2019, before the COVID-19 pandemic, and monthly ridership is included for trend analyses.

## Settings
```{r}
#| label: group 2 settings

# NITA (formerly RTAMS) CTA ridership and GIS files, downloaded from
# https://datahub.nita.illinois.gov/media/datasets/cta-ridership and saved in the
# data directory. When NITA posts newer files, save them and update the names below.
g2_file_bus_ridership <- file.path(data_dir, "CTA_Average_Bus_Ridership_1999_2026.xlsx")
g2_file_rail_ridership <- file.path(data_dir, "CTA_Average_Rail_Station_Ridership_1999_2026.csv")
g2_file_bus_routes <- file.path(data_dir, "CTA_Bus_Routes.shp")
g2_file_rail_stations <- file.path(data_dir, "CTA_RAIL_STATIONS.shp")
g2_file_rail_lines <- file.path(data_dir, "CTA_RAIL_LINES.shp")

# CTA bus stops (Chicago Data Portal); $limit raises the portal's default of 1,000 rows
url_bus_stops <- "https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/hvnx-qtky.geojson?$limit=50000"

# Ashland Avenue bus routes: 9 Ashland and X9 Ashland Express
g2_routes <- c("9", "X9")

# rail stations within this distance (feet) of the Ashland routes: a quarter mile
g2_station_buffer_ft <- 1320

# pre-pandemic comparison year and first year of monthly ridership kept
g2_baseline_year <- 2019
g2_trend_start <- 2012

# output files
g2_gpkg <- file.path(data_dir, "group02_ashland_brt.gpkg")
g2_rdata <- file.path(data_dir, "group02_ashland_brt.RData")
```

## Data sources
- [NITA CTA ridership](https://datahub.nita.illinois.gov/media/datasets/cta-ridership) (Northeastern Illinois Transportation Analytics, formerly RTAMS), saved in `projects/data/`:
  - `CTA_Average_Bus_Ridership_1999_2026.xlsx`: average daily boardings by bus route, month and day type (weekday, Saturday, Sunday/holiday), January 1999 to June 2026. A rider who transfers between two routes is counted on both.
  - `CTA_Average_Rail_Station_Ridership_1999_2026.csv`: total and average daily entries by rail station, month and day type, January 1999 to June 2026.
  - `CTA_Bus_Routes.shp`: current bus route alignments (one line per route), with route number (`ROUTE`), name and type (`KEY` or `SUPPORT` route).
  - `CTA_RAIL_STATIONS.shp` and `CTA_RAIL_LINES.shp`: rail stations and lines. Station ids (`STATION_ID`) match the rail ridership file's `RIDERSHIP_ID`.
- [CTA Bus Stops](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Transportation/CTA-Bus-Stops/hvnx-qtky) (Chicago Data Portal): bus stop locations and the routes serving each stop. The download is also saved as a cache file.

## Functions
```{r}
#| label: group 2 functions

# NITA ridership files (CSV or Excel) are read as text and their columns
# standardized; each element of lookup lists the column names a standard column
# may have in the file. Columns in optional may be missing (set to NA).
fx_read_nita_ridership <- function(file, lookup, optional = c("name", "total_rides")) {
  ridership <- if (str_detect(file, "\\.xlsx?$")) {
    read_excel(file, col_types = "text")
  } else {
    read_csv(file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
  }
  names(ridership) <- str_to_upper(str_trim(str_remove(names(ridership), "^﻿")))
  for (new in names(lookup)) {
    old <- intersect(lookup[[new]], names(ridership))[1]
    if (!is.na(old)) names(ridership)[names(ridership) == old] <- new
  }
  missing <- setdiff(setdiff(names(lookup), optional), names(ridership))
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    stop("Columns not found in ", file, ": ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         "\nColumns in the file: ", paste(names(ridership), collapse = ", "),
         "\nAdd the file's column names to the lookup.")
  }
  for (col in setdiff(optional, names(ridership))) ridership[[col]] <- NA_character_
  ridership %>%
    transmute(id = str_trim(id),
              name = str_trim(name),
              year = as.integer(year),
              month = as.integer(month),
              year_month = make_date(year, month, 1),
              day_type = str_trim(day_type),
              day_key = case_when(str_detect(str_to_lower(day_type), "^w") ~ "weekday",
                                  str_detect(str_to_lower(day_type), "^sa") ~ "saturday",
                                  TRUE ~ "sunday_holiday"),
              total_rides = parse_number(total_rides),
              daily_avg_rides = parse_number(daily_avg_rides)) %>%
    drop_na(id, year_month)
}

# current (latest 12 months) and baseline-year average daily rides by day type,
# current weekday rides as a percent of baseline weekday rides, and rank by
# current weekday rides among all ids (routes or stations) in the file
fx_ridership_summary <- function(ridership, baseline_year) {
  latest <- max(ridership$year_month)
  current_months <- seq(latest %m-% months(11), latest, by = "month")
  ridership %>%
    group_by(id, day_key) %>%
    summarise(current = mean(daily_avg_rides[year_month %in% current_months]),
              baseline = mean(daily_avg_rides[year == baseline_year]),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(across(c(current, baseline), ~ if_else(is.nan(.x), NA_real_, round(.x)))) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = day_key, values_from = c(current, baseline),
                names_glue = "avg_{day_key}_{.value}") %>%
    select(id, avg_weekday_current, avg_saturday_current, avg_sunday_holiday_current,
           avg_weekday_baseline) %>%
    mutate(weekday_pct_of_baseline = round(100 * avg_weekday_current / avg_weekday_baseline, 1),
           weekday_rank = min_rank(desc(avg_weekday_current)))
}
```

## Bus routes
*Connecting* routes are bus routes whose alignments cross or overlap the Ashland routes. `overlap_mi` is the length (miles) of each route that runs along the Ashland routes, so routes that share Ashland Avenue for some distance can be distinguished from routes that simply cross it.

```{r}
#| label: group 2 bus routes

g2_bus_routes_all <- st_read(g2_file_bus_routes, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_transform(3435) %>%
  transmute(route_id = str_trim(ROUTE),
            route_name = str_to_title(NAME),
            route_type = str_to_lower(TYPE))

# Ashland routes, combined into a single line, and a narrow (100 ft) buffer used
# to measure how far other routes run along Ashland
g2_ashland_line <- g2_bus_routes_all %>%
  filter(route_id %in% g2_routes) %>%
  st_union()
if (length(g2_ashland_line) == 0 || st_is_empty(g2_ashland_line)) {
  stop("None of the Ashland routes (", paste(g2_routes, collapse = ", "), ") are in ", g2_file_bus_routes)
}
g2_ashland_narrow <- st_buffer(g2_ashland_line, 100)

g2_bus_routes <- g2_bus_routes_all %>%
  st_filter(st_buffer(g2_ashland_line, 50)) %>%
  mutate(route_role = if_else(route_id %in% g2_routes, "Ashland", "connecting"),
         route_mi = round(as.numeric(st_length(geometry)) / 5280, 1),
         overlap_mi = map_dbl(geometry, function(g) {
           sum(as.numeric(st_length(st_intersection(st_sfc(g, crs = 3435), g2_ashland_narrow))))
         }),
         overlap_mi = round(overlap_mi / 5280, 1))
```

## Bus route ridership
```{r}
#| label: group 2 bus ridership

g2_bus_all <- fx_read_nita_ridership(
  g2_file_bus_ridership,
  lookup = list(id = c("ROUTE", "ROUTE_ID", "RT"),
                name = c("ROUTE_NAME", "ROUTENAME", "NAME"),
                year = "YEAR",
                month = "MONTH",
                day_type = c("DAY_TYPE", "DAYTYPE"),
                total_rides = c("TOTAL_RIDES", "RIDES"),
                daily_avg_rides = c("AVG_RIDES", "DAILY_AVG_RIDES", "AVG_DAILY_RIDES")))

# latest month of bus ridership
g2_bus_through <- max(g2_bus_all$year_month)

# summary computed for all routes, so ranks are among all CTA bus routes
ashland_bus_routes <- g2_bus_routes %>%
  left_join(fx_ridership_summary(g2_bus_all, g2_baseline_year), by = c("route_id" = "id")) %>%
  select(route_id, route_name, route_type, route_role, route_mi, overlap_mi,
         avg_weekday_current, avg_saturday_current, avg_sunday_holiday_current,
         avg_weekday_baseline, weekday_pct_of_baseline, weekday_rank) %>%
  arrange(route_role, desc(avg_weekday_current))

# monthly ridership for the Ashland and connecting routes (the bus file has
# average daily rides only)
ashland_bus_ridership <- g2_bus_all %>%
  filter(id %in% ashland_bus_routes$route_id, year >= g2_trend_start) %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(ashland_bus_routes) %>% select(route_id, route_name, route_role),
            by = c("id" = "route_id")) %>%
  select(route_id = id, route_name, route_role, year, month, year_month, day_type,
         daily_avg_rides) %>%
  arrange(route_id, year_month, day_type)
```

## Bus stops
Bus stops served by the Ashland routes are selected using the routes listed for each stop in the portal's bus stop data. If that column cannot be found, stops within 100 feet of the Ashland routes are selected instead.

```{r}
#| label: group 2 bus stops

g2_stops_all <- read_portal_geojson(url_bus_stops, file.path(data_dir, "bus_stops_cache.geojson")) %>%
  st_transform(3435)
names(g2_stops_all) <- str_to_lower(names(g2_stops_all))
st_geometry(g2_stops_all) <- "geometry"

# column listing the routes serving each stop (e.g., "9,X9,66")
g2_routes_col <- str_subset(names(g2_stops_all), "^routes")[1]

if (!is.na(g2_routes_col)) {
  ashland_bus_stops <- g2_stops_all %>%
    mutate(routes = str_squish(.data[[g2_routes_col]])) %>%
    filter(map_lgl(str_split(coalesce(routes, ""), "[,;[:space:]]+"), ~ any(.x %in% g2_routes)))
} else {
  message("No routes column found in the bus stop data; selecting stops within 100 feet of the Ashland routes")
  ashland_bus_stops <- g2_stops_all %>%
    st_filter(g2_ashland_narrow) %>%
    mutate(routes = NA_character_)
}

g2_stop_coords <- st_coordinates(st_transform(ashland_bus_stops, 4326))
ashland_bus_stops <- ashland_bus_stops %>%
  mutate(stop_lon = g2_stop_coords[, "X"],
         stop_lat = g2_stop_coords[, "Y"]) %>%
  select(any_of(c(stop_id = "systemstop", stop_name = "public_nam", street = "street",
                  cross_street = "cross_st", direction = "dir")),
         routes, stop_lat, stop_lon) %>%
  st_join(select(community_areas, comarea_id, comarea_name)) %>%
  arrange(desc(stop_lat))

rm(g2_stops_all, g2_stop_coords)
```

## Rail stations and ridership
CTA rail stations within a quarter mile (`g2_station_buffer_ft`) of the Ashland routes are selected, with their distance from the routes.

```{r}
#| label: group 2 rail ridership

line_names <- c(BL = "Blue", BR = "Brown", GR = "Green", ML = "Multi",
                OR = "Orange", PK = "Pink", PR = "Purple", RD = "Red", YL = "Yellow")

g2_rail_all <- fx_read_nita_ridership(
  g2_file_rail_ridership,
  lookup = list(id = c("RIDERSHIP_ID", "STATION_ID"),
                name = c("NAME", "STATION_NAME", "STATIONNAME"),
                year = "YEAR",
                month = "MONTH",
                day_type = c("DAY_TYPE", "DAYTYPE"),
                total_rides = c("TOTAL_RIDES", "RIDES"),
                daily_avg_rides = c("DAILY_AVG_RIDES", "AVG_RIDES", "AVG_DAILY_RIDES")))

# latest month of rail ridership
g2_rail_through <- max(g2_rail_all$year_month)

ashland_rail_stations <- st_read(g2_file_rail_stations, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_transform(3435) %>%
  transmute(station_id = as.character(as.numeric(STATION_ID)),
            station_name = LONGNAME,
            station_line = unname(line_names[LEGEND])) %>%
  mutate(dist_ashland_ft = round(as.numeric(st_distance(geometry, g2_ashland_line)))) %>%
  filter(dist_ashland_ft <= g2_station_buffer_ft) %>%
  st_join(select(community_areas, comarea_id, comarea_name), join = st_nearest_feature) %>%
  left_join(fx_ridership_summary(g2_rail_all, g2_baseline_year), by = c("station_id" = "id")) %>%
  arrange(desc(st_coordinates(geometry)[, "Y"]))

# monthly ridership for the stations near Ashland
ashland_rail_ridership <- g2_rail_all %>%
  filter(id %in% ashland_rail_stations$station_id, year >= g2_trend_start) %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(ashland_rail_stations) %>% select(station_id, station_name, station_line),
            by = c("id" = "station_id")) %>%
  select(station_id = id, station_name, station_line, year, month, year_month, day_type,
         total_rides, daily_avg_rides) %>%
  arrange(station_id, year_month, day_type)

# all CTA rail lines, for reference on maps
cta_rail_lines <- st_read(g2_file_rail_lines, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_transform(3435) %>%
  select(rail_line = COLOR)
```

## Community areas along Ashland Avenue
```{r}
#| label: group 2 community areas

ashland_community_areas <- community_areas %>%
  inner_join(ashland_bus_stops %>%
               st_drop_geometry() %>%
               count(comarea_id, name = "n_bus_stops"),
             by = "comarea_id") %>%
  left_join(ashland_rail_stations %>%
              st_drop_geometry() %>%
              count(comarea_id, name = "n_rail_stations"),
            by = "comarea_id") %>%
  mutate(n_rail_stations = replace_na(n_rail_stations, 0L),
         area_sqmi = round(area_sqmi, 2)) %>%
  arrange(comarea_id)
```

## Save datasets
Spatial layers are saved in WGS84 (epsg:4326), as for Group 1.

```{r}
#| label: group 2 save datasets

ashland_bus_routes <- st_transform(ashland_bus_routes, 4326)
ashland_bus_stops <- st_transform(ashland_bus_stops, 4326)
ashland_rail_stations <- st_transform(ashland_rail_stations, 4326)
ashland_community_areas <- st_transform(ashland_community_areas, 4326)
cta_rail_lines <- st_transform(cta_rail_lines, 4326)

# GeoPackage (one layer per dataset)
if (file.exists(g2_gpkg)) file.remove(g2_gpkg)
st_write(ashland_bus_routes, g2_gpkg, layer = "ashland_bus_routes", quiet = TRUE)
st_write(ashland_bus_stops, g2_gpkg, layer = "ashland_bus_stops", quiet = TRUE)
st_write(ashland_rail_stations, g2_gpkg, layer = "ashland_rail_stations", quiet = TRUE)
st_write(ashland_community_areas, g2_gpkg, layer = "ashland_community_areas", quiet = TRUE)
st_write(cta_rail_lines, g2_gpkg, layer = "cta_rail_lines", quiet = TRUE)

# CSV tables
write_csv(st_drop_geometry(ashland_bus_routes), file.path(data_dir, "group02_ashland_bus_routes.csv"))
write_csv(st_drop_geometry(ashland_bus_stops), file.path(data_dir, "group02_ashland_bus_stops.csv"))
write_csv(st_drop_geometry(ashland_rail_stations), file.path(data_dir, "group02_ashland_rail_stations.csv"))
write_csv(ashland_bus_ridership, file.path(data_dir, "group02_ashland_bus_ridership_monthly.csv"))
write_csv(ashland_rail_ridership, file.path(data_dir, "group02_ashland_rail_ridership_monthly.csv"))

# R datasets
save_with_community_areas(c("ashland_bus_routes", "ashland_bus_stops", "ashland_rail_stations",
                            "ashland_community_areas", "cta_rail_lines", "ashland_bus_ridership",
                            "ashland_rail_ridership", "g2_bus_through", "g2_rail_through",
                            "g2_baseline_year"),
                          g2_rdata)
```

## Dataset descriptions
Ridership columns are the same for bus routes and rail stations. *Current* is the latest 12 months of ridership available (July 2025 to June 2026 in the 1999-2026 files; see `g2_bus_through` and `g2_rail_through`); *baseline* is `g2_baseline_year` (2019).

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `avg_weekday_current`, `avg_saturday_current`, `avg_sunday_holiday_current` | Average daily rides (bus boardings or rail station entries) by day type, latest 12 months |
| `avg_weekday_baseline` | Average weekday rides in 2019 |
| `weekday_pct_of_baseline` | Current weekday rides as a percent of 2019 weekday rides (ridership recovery) |
| `weekday_rank` | Rank by current average weekday rides among all CTA bus routes (bus) or rail stations (rail); 1 = busiest |

### `ashland_bus_routes` (lines, one row per route)
The Ashland routes (9 and X9) and the bus routes that cross or connect with them, with `route_id`, `route_name`, `route_type` (CTA `key` or `support` route), `route_role` (`Ashland` or `connecting`), route length (`route_mi`), miles running along the Ashland routes (`overlap_mi`), and the ridership columns above. Ridership is for each entire route, not only the part on or near Ashland Avenue.

### `ashland_rail_stations` (points, one row per station)
CTA rail stations within a quarter mile of the Ashland routes, with `station_id`, `station_name`, `station_line` (`Multi` for stations served by more than one line), distance from the Ashland routes (`dist_ashland_ft`), community area, and the ridership columns above. Rail ridership counts entries at each station; riders transferring between lines within a station are not counted again.

### `ashland_bus_stops` (points, one row per stop)
Bus stops served by the Ashland routes, with the stop id and name, street, cross street, direction, the routes serving the stop (`routes`), latitude and longitude, and community area. Stops have no ridership (see limitations); they can be used to measure stop spacing (a key difference between local bus and BRT service), identify transfer points and summarize the population or destinations near the corridor.

### `ashland_community_areas` (polygons, one row per community area)
Community areas with Ashland bus stops, with population, land area, and the number of Ashland bus stops (`n_bus_stops`) and nearby rail stations (`n_rail_stations`).

### `cta_rail_lines` (lines)
All CTA rail lines (`rail_line`), for reference on maps.

### `ashland_bus_ridership` and `ashland_rail_ridership` (tables, one row per route or station, month and day type)
Monthly ridership since `g2_trend_start` (2012) for the routes and stations above: average daily rides (`daily_avg_rides`) by `day_type`, and, for rail stations, total rides (`total_rides`).

## How these datasets may inform the project
- **Demand for BRT.** Use `weekday_rank` and `avg_weekday_current` to show how the Ashland routes compare with other CTA bus routes; high ridership on a long, continuous arterial is a common argument for BRT. Compare current ridership with 2019 (`weekday_pct_of_baseline`) and with other routes' recovery. The X9 express, which skips most local stops, offers a useful comparison with route 9 local service.
- **Trends.** Plot the monthly tables to show ridership on the Ashland routes and nearby rail stations since 2012, including the period when CTA and the city proposed BRT on Ashland Avenue in the 2010s, the pandemic decline and the recovery since.
- **Network connections.** Connecting routes and rail stations show where Ashland riders can transfer; ridership at those routes and stations suggests where BRT stations might be located and how a faster Ashland service could connect neighborhoods with the rail network.
- **Stop spacing and station locations.** Measure distances between consecutive `ashland_bus_stops` (by direction) and compare with typical BRT station spacing; locate potential BRT stations at rail stations and busy connecting routes.
- **Who is served.** Join `ashland_community_areas` (by `comarea_id`) with Health Atlas indicators (e.g., poverty, ease of walking to transit; Exercises #3 and #4) or census data on car ownership and commuting to describe the neighborhoods along the corridor.

## Limitations
- **Route-level bus ridership.** NITA bus ridership is by route and month, not by stop, direction or segment, so it cannot show where along Ashland riders board.
- **Average daily rides only for buses.** The bus ridership file has average daily rides but not monthly totals.
- **Boardings, not riders.** Bus boardings and rail entries count trips, not unique riders, and transfers between buses are counted on each route.
- **Current alignments.** Route alignments and stops reflect current service; routes that no longer operate are not included in `ashland_bus_routes`, though their historical ridership is in the bus ridership file.

# Group 3: Pedestrian safety near CTA rail stations
## Project overview
Group 3 is mapping pedestrian crashes near CTA rail stations. Station areas concentrate people walking to and from trains and buses, often across busy streets, so they are a useful place to examine pedestrian safety. The datasets below use the same Chicago Data Portal crash data and years as Group 1, and the CTA rail stations and rail ridership from Group 2 (run the Group 2 section first), to count pedestrian crashes within three distances of each station.

## Settings
```{r}
#| label: group 3 settings

# same years as Group 1
g3_years <- g1_years
g3_where_dates <- g1_where_dates

# distances (feet) from each station
g3_radii_ft <- c(25, 50, 100)

# output files
g3_gpkg <- file.path(data_dir, "group03_pedestrian_crashes_stations.gpkg")
g3_rdata <- file.path(data_dir, "group03_pedestrian_crashes_stations.RData")
```

## Data sources
- [Traffic Crashes - Crashes](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Transportation/Traffic-Crashes-Crashes/85ca-t3if/about_data) and [Traffic Crashes - People](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Transportation/Traffic-Crashes-People/u6pd-qa9d/about_data) (see Group 1). A crash is identified as a **pedestrian crash** when its first crash type is `PEDESTRIAN` *or* at least one person involved was a pedestrian (`person_type = 'PEDESTRIAN'`).
- CTA rail stations and rail station ridership from NITA (see Group 2).

## Download pedestrian crash records
```{r}
#| label: group 3 download crash records

# pedestrians involved in crashes
g3_people <- read_portal_csv(
  soql_url(id_people,
           `$where` = paste(g3_where_dates, "AND person_type = 'PEDESTRIAN'"),
           `$limit` = soql_limit),
  file.path(data_dir, "group03_people_pedestrian_cache.csv"))

# crashes with a first crash type of PEDESTRIAN
g3_crashes_pedestrian <- read_portal_csv(
  soql_url(id_crashes,
           `$where` = paste(g3_where_dates, "AND first_crash_type = 'PEDESTRIAN'"),
           `$limit` = soql_limit),
  file.path(data_dir, "group03_crashes_pedestrian_cache.csv"))

# other crashes involving a pedestrian
g3_crashes_other <- read_portal_ids(
  id_crashes, "crash_record_id",
  setdiff(unique(g3_people$crash_record_id), g3_crashes_pedestrian$crash_record_id),
  file.path(data_dir, "group03_crashes_other_cache.csv"))

g3_crashes_raw <- bind_rows(g3_crashes_pedestrian, g3_crashes_other) %>%
  distinct(crash_record_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

## Pedestrian crash points
Pedestrian records are summarized by crash (number of pedestrians involved, killed, seriously injured and injured, and the injury classification, age, sex, action and location of the most severely injured pedestrian), joined to the crash records, located with their latitude and longitude, and attributed with their community area and nearest CTA rail station.

```{r}
#| label: group 3 pedestrian crash points

g3_pedestrians <- g3_people %>%
  mutate(injury = factor(injury_classification, levels = injury_levels, ordered = TRUE),
         age = as.numeric(age),
         age = if_else(age <= 0 | age > 110, NA_real_, age)) %>%
  arrange(crash_record_id, desc(injury)) %>%
  group_by(crash_record_id) %>%
  summarise(n_pedestrians = n(),
            n_pedestrians_killed = sum(injury == "FATAL", na.rm = TRUE),
            n_pedestrians_seriously_injured = sum(injury == "INCAPACITATING INJURY", na.rm = TRUE),
            n_pedestrians_injured = sum(injury >= "NONINCAPACITATING INJURY", na.rm = TRUE),
            pedestrian_injury = as.character(first(injury)),
            pedestrian_age = first(age),
            pedestrian_sex = first(sex),
            pedestrian_action = first(pedpedal_action),
            pedestrian_location = first(pedpedal_location),
            .groups = "drop")

g3_crashes <- g3_crashes_raw %>%
  mutate(ped_source = case_when(
    first_crash_type == "PEDESTRIAN" & crash_record_id %in% g3_people$crash_record_id ~ "both",
    first_crash_type == "PEDESTRIAN" ~ "first crash type",
    TRUE ~ "pedestrian record")) %>%
  select(crash_record_id, crash_date, posted_speed_limit, traffic_control_device,
         weather_condition, lighting_condition, first_crash_type, trafficway_type,
         roadway_surface_cond, crash_type, intersection_related_i, hit_and_run_i,
         prim_contributory_cause, sec_contributory_cause, street_no, street_direction,
         street_name, num_units, most_severe_injury, injuries_total, injuries_fatal,
         injuries_incapacitating, latitude, longitude, ped_source) %>%
  mutate(crash_date = ymd_hms(crash_date, tz = "America/Chicago", truncated = 3),
         crash_year = year(crash_date),
         crash_month = month(crash_date),
         crash_hour = hour(crash_date),
         crash_day_of_week = wday(crash_date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
         across(c(posted_speed_limit, num_units, injuries_total, injuries_fatal,
                  injuries_incapacitating, latitude, longitude), as.numeric),
         across(c(intersection_related_i, hit_and_run_i), ~ replace_na(.x, "N")),
         ksi_crash = injuries_fatal + injuries_incapacitating > 0) %>%
  left_join(g3_pedestrians, by = "crash_record_id") %>%
  mutate(across(c(n_pedestrians, n_pedestrians_killed, n_pedestrians_seriously_injured,
                  n_pedestrians_injured), ~ replace_na(.x, 0L))) %>%
  filter(crash_year %in% g3_years) %>%
  arrange(crash_date)

# crashes without usable coordinates
g3_crashes_unlocated <- g3_crashes %>%
  filter(is.na(latitude) | is.na(longitude) | latitude == 0 | longitude == 0)

# CTA rail stations (Group 2 file) with current and 2019 ridership (Group 2 summary)
g3_stations <- st_read(g2_file_rail_stations, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_transform(3435) %>%
  transmute(station_id = as.character(as.numeric(STATION_ID)),
            station_name = LONGNAME,
            station_line = unname(line_names[LEGEND])) %>%
  st_join(select(community_areas, comarea_id, comarea_name), join = st_nearest_feature) %>%
  left_join(fx_ridership_summary(g2_rail_all, g2_baseline_year) %>%
              select(id, avg_weekday_current, avg_weekday_baseline, weekday_rank),
            by = c("station_id" = "id"))

pedestrian_crashes <- g3_crashes %>%
  anti_join(g3_crashes_unlocated, by = "crash_record_id") %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) %>%
  st_transform(3435)

# community area (nearest within g1_snap_ft, as for Group 1)
nearest_ca <- st_nearest_feature(pedestrian_crashes, community_areas)
nearest_ft <- as.numeric(st_distance(pedestrian_crashes, community_areas[nearest_ca, ], by_element = TRUE))

# nearest CTA rail station and distance (feet)
nearest_station <- st_nearest_feature(pedestrian_crashes, g3_stations)

pedestrian_crashes <- pedestrian_crashes %>%
  mutate(comarea_id = if_else(nearest_ft <= g1_snap_ft,
                              community_areas$comarea_id[nearest_ca], NA_real_),
         station_id = g3_stations$station_id[nearest_station],
         station_name = g3_stations$station_name[nearest_station],
         station_dist_ft = round(as.numeric(st_distance(geometry, g3_stations[nearest_station, ],
                                                         by_element = TRUE)), 1)) %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(community_areas) %>% select(comarea_id, comarea_name),
            by = "comarea_id") %>%
  relocate(comarea_id, comarea_name, station_id, station_name, station_dist_ft, .before = ped_source)

# flags for crashes within each distance of the nearest station (e.g., within_25ft)
for (r in g3_radii_ft) {
  pedestrian_crashes[[paste0("within_", r, "ft")]] <- pedestrian_crashes$station_dist_ft <= r
}

rm(nearest_ca, nearest_ft, nearest_station, r)
```

## Pedestrian crashes by station and distance
Crashes are counted within each distance (`g3_radii_ft`) of each station. Counts are cumulative: crashes within 25 feet are also counted within 50 and 100 feet. A crash within the distance of two stations is counted for both.

```{r}
#| label: group 3 crashes by station

# crash-station pairs within the largest distance
g3_pairs <- st_is_within_distance(pedestrian_crashes, g3_stations, dist = max(g3_radii_ft))
g3_near <- tibble(crash_i = rep(seq_along(g3_pairs), lengths(g3_pairs)),
                  station_i = unlist(g3_pairs)) %>%
  mutate(crash_record_id = pedestrian_crashes$crash_record_id[crash_i],
         station_id = g3_stations$station_id[station_i],
         dist_ft = as.numeric(st_distance(pedestrian_crashes[crash_i, ], g3_stations[station_i, ],
                                          by_element = TRUE))) %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(pedestrian_crashes) %>%
              select(crash_record_id, crash_year, ksi_crash, n_pedestrians_injured,
                     n_pedestrians_seriously_injured, n_pedestrians_killed),
            by = "crash_record_id") %>%
  crossing(radius_ft = g3_radii_ft) %>%
  filter(dist_ft <= radius_ft)

g3_count_cols <- c("crashes", "crashes_ksi", "pedestrians_injured",
                   "pedestrians_seriously_injured", "pedestrians_killed")

fx_count_ped_crashes <- function(near, ...) {
  near %>%
    group_by(station_id, radius_ft, ...) %>%
    summarise(crashes = n(),
              crashes_ksi = sum(ksi_crash, na.rm = TRUE),
              pedestrians_injured = sum(n_pedestrians_injured),
              pedestrians_seriously_injured = sum(n_pedestrians_seriously_injured),
              pedestrians_killed = sum(n_pedestrians_killed),
              .groups = "drop")
}

# one row per station, distance and year (zeros where no crashes occurred)
station_ped_crashes_year <- fx_count_ped_crashes(g3_near, crash_year) %>%
  complete(station_id = g3_stations$station_id, radius_ft = g3_radii_ft, crash_year = g3_years) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(g3_count_cols), ~ replace_na(.x, 0L))) %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(g3_stations) %>% select(station_id, station_name, station_line),
            by = "station_id") %>%
  select(station_id, station_name, station_line, radius_ft, crash_year, all_of(g3_count_cols)) %>%
  arrange(station_id, radius_ft, crash_year)

# one row per station: five-year totals within each distance as columns
# (e.g., crashes_25ft, crashes_ksi_100ft), with ridership and a crash rate per
# 1,000 average weekday entries (100 ft)
station_ped_crashes <- g3_stations %>%
  left_join(fx_count_ped_crashes(g3_near) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = radius_ft, values_from = all_of(g3_count_cols),
                          names_glue = "{.value}_{radius_ft}ft"),
            by = "station_id") %>%
  mutate(across(matches("_\\d+ft$"), ~ replace_na(.x, 0L)),
         crashes_per_1k_riders = round(.data[[paste0("crashes_", max(g3_radii_ft), "ft")]] /
                                         avg_weekday_current * 1000, 2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(.data[[paste0("crashes_", max(g3_radii_ft), "ft")]]))

# station buffers (one polygon per station and distance), for mapping
station_buffers <- map(g3_radii_ft, function(r) {
  g3_stations %>%
    select(station_id, station_name) %>%
    mutate(radius_ft = r) %>%
    st_buffer(r)
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  left_join(fx_count_ped_crashes(g3_near) %>% select(station_id, radius_ft, crashes),
            by = c("station_id", "radius_ft")) %>%
  mutate(crashes = replace_na(crashes, 0L))

rm(g3_pairs)
```

## Checks
```{r}
#| label: group 3 checks

# crashes by identification source, and crashes without coordinates
count(g3_crashes, ped_source)
nrow(g3_crashes_unlocated)

# crashes within each distance of a station (each crash counted once)
sapply(g3_radii_ft, function(r) sum(pedestrian_crashes$station_dist_ft <= r)) %>%
  setNames(paste0(g3_radii_ft, "ft"))

# stations with the most pedestrian crashes within the largest distance
station_ped_crashes %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(station_name, station_line, starts_with("crashes_"), avg_weekday_current) %>%
  head(20)

# stations without ridership (ids that do not match the ridership file)
filter(station_ped_crashes, is.na(avg_weekday_current))$station_name

# pedestrian crashes within the largest distance of a station
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = community_areas, fill = "grey95", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = cta_rail_lines, color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = station_ped_crashes,
          aes(size = .data[[paste0("crashes_", max(g3_radii_ft), "ft")]]),
          color = "#d62728", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_size_area(name = sprintf("Pedestrian crashes\nwithin %d ft", max(g3_radii_ft))) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Pedestrian crashes near CTA rail stations, %d-%d", min(g3_years), max(g3_years))) +
  theme_void()
```

## Save datasets
```{r}
#| label: group 3 save datasets

pedestrian_crashes <- st_transform(pedestrian_crashes, 4326)
station_ped_crashes <- st_transform(station_ped_crashes, 4326)
station_buffers <- st_transform(station_buffers, 4326)

# GeoPackage (one layer per dataset; cta_rail_lines from Group 2)
if (file.exists(g3_gpkg)) file.remove(g3_gpkg)
st_write(pedestrian_crashes, g3_gpkg, layer = "pedestrian_crashes", quiet = TRUE)
st_write(station_ped_crashes, g3_gpkg, layer = "station_ped_crashes", quiet = TRUE)
st_write(station_buffers, g3_gpkg, layer = "station_buffers", quiet = TRUE)
st_write(cta_rail_lines, g3_gpkg, layer = "cta_rail_lines", quiet = TRUE)

# CSV tables (crash points include latitude and longitude)
write_csv(st_drop_geometry(pedestrian_crashes), file.path(data_dir, "group03_pedestrian_crashes.csv"))
write_csv(st_drop_geometry(station_ped_crashes), file.path(data_dir, "group03_station_ped_crashes.csv"))
write_csv(station_ped_crashes_year, file.path(data_dir, "group03_station_ped_crashes_year.csv"))

# R datasets
save_with_community_areas(c("pedestrian_crashes", "station_ped_crashes", "station_ped_crashes_year",
                            "station_buffers", "cta_rail_lines", "g3_years", "g3_radii_ft"),
                          g3_rdata)
```

## Dataset descriptions
### `pedestrian_crashes` (points, one row per crash)
Pedestrian crashes reported by CPD on city streets, `r min(g3_years)`-`r max(g3_years)`, citywide. Crash columns are the same as Group 1's `bike_crashes` (date and time, speed limit, traffic control, conditions, first crash type, contributing causes, address, crash-level injuries, `ksi_crash`, latitude and longitude, community area), plus:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `n_pedestrians`, `n_pedestrians_injured`, `n_pedestrians_seriously_injured`, `n_pedestrians_killed` | Pedestrians involved, injured (non-incapacitating or worse), seriously injured and killed |
| `pedestrian_injury`, `pedestrian_age`, `pedestrian_sex` | Injury classification, age and sex of the most severely injured pedestrian |
| `pedestrian_action`, `pedestrian_location` | What the pedestrian was doing (e.g., crossing with or against the signal) and where (e.g., in crosswalk, not in crosswalk) |
| `station_id`, `station_name`, `station_dist_ft` | Nearest CTA rail station and distance (feet) |
| `within_25ft`, `within_50ft`, `within_100ft` | Crash within each distance of the nearest station (TRUE/FALSE) |
| `ped_source` | How the crash was identified: `first crash type`, `pedestrian record` or `both` |

### `station_ped_crashes` (points, one row per CTA rail station)
Station id, name, line and community area; current (latest 12 months) and 2019 average weekday entries and rank (as in Group 2); and five-year totals within each distance, named by distance (e.g., `crashes_25ft`, `crashes_50ft`, `crashes_100ft`):

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `crashes_*ft` | Pedestrian crashes |
| `crashes_ksi_*ft` | Crashes in which someone was killed or seriously injured |
| `pedestrians_injured_*ft`, `pedestrians_seriously_injured_*ft`, `pedestrians_killed_*ft` | Pedestrians injured, seriously injured and killed |
| `crashes_per_1k_riders` | Crashes within the largest distance per 1,000 current average weekday entries |

### `station_ped_crashes_year` (table, one row per station, distance and year)
The same counts by year (`radius_ft`, `crash_year`), with zeros where no crashes occurred.

### `station_buffers` (polygons, one row per station and distance)
Circles of each radius around each station, with the number of crashes within each, for mapping.

## How these datasets may inform the project
- **Where.** Map `station_ped_crashes` (sized or colored by crashes) with `pedestrian_crashes` and `station_buffers` to identify the stations with the most pedestrian crashes nearby, and compare lines and parts of the city.
- **Distance.** Compare counts at 25, 50 and 100 feet to see whether crashes cluster right at station entrances or on the surrounding streets.
- **Exposure.** Busier stations bring more pedestrians; compare crash counts with `avg_weekday_current` or use `crashes_per_1k_riders` to identify stations with more crashes than their ridership would suggest.
- **Conditions and severity.** Use `pedestrian_action`, `pedestrian_location`, `lighting_condition`, `crash_hour`, `traffic_control_device` and `posted_speed_limit` to compare crashes near stations with crashes elsewhere in the city, and to ask which street designs near stations (e.g., wide arterials, signals, crosswalks) are associated with severe crashes.
- **Trends.** Use `station_ped_crashes_year` to see whether crashes near particular stations are rising or falling, e.g., before and after street safety improvements.

## Limitations
- **Station locations are points.** Each station is a single point, but stations, especially subway stations and stations with several entrances, can span a block or more, and crash locations are approximate (often geocoded to the nearest intersection or address). Very short distances (25 and 50 feet) may capture few crashes; increase `g3_radii_ft` (e.g., 250 or 500 feet, roughly one or two blocks) if needed.
- **Station list.** The NITA station file dates from 2020, so stations opened since then are not included.
- **Underreporting and coverage.** As for Group 1, only crashes reported to CPD on city streets are included.

# Group 4: Motorcycle fatalities in the city of Chicago
## Project overview
Group 4 is studying motorcycle fatalities in Chicago. The datasets below locate every fatal crash involving a motorcycle over the same five years as Group 1, and summarize fatalities citywide and by community area and year, so that trends and geographic patterns can be mapped and compared.

## Settings
```{r}
#| label: group 4 settings

# same years as Group 1
g4_years <- g1_years
g4_where_dates <- g1_where_dates

# Traffic Crashes - Vehicles dataset (one record per vehicle or other unit)
id_vehicles <- "68nd-jvt3"

# motorcycle vehicle types (Vehicles dataset vehicle_type), matched as SoQL patterns:
# motorcycles of all sizes, motor driven cycles and autocycles; mopeds and motorized
# bicycles are included but labeled separately (vehicle_class) so they can be excluded
g4_vehicle_patterns <- c("%MOTORCYCLE%", "%MOTOR DRIVEN%", "%AUTOCYCLE%", "%MOPED%")

# output files
g4_gpkg <- file.path(data_dir, "group04_motorcycle_fatalities.gpkg")
g4_rdata <- file.path(data_dir, "group04_motorcycle_fatalities.RData")
```

## Data sources
Three related Chicago Data Portal datasets, joined by `crash_record_id` (and `vehicle_id`):

- [Traffic Crashes - Vehicles](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Transportation/Traffic-Crashes-Vehicles/68nd-jvt3/about_data): one record per vehicle in a crash, with its vehicle type. Motorcycle crashes are crashes involving at least one vehicle of a motorcycle type (`g4_vehicle_patterns`).
- [Traffic Crashes - Crashes](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Transportation/Traffic-Crashes-Crashes/85ca-t3if/about_data) (see Group 1): crashes with at least one fatality (`injuries_fatal > 0`) are downloaded and matched with the motorcycle crashes.
- [Traffic Crashes - People](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Transportation/Traffic-Crashes-People/u6pd-qa9d/about_data): the people involved in the fatal motorcycle crashes. People in a motorcycle (`vehicle_id`) who were killed are counted as *motorcyclists killed*; anyone else killed (e.g., pedestrians or people in other vehicles) is counted as *others killed*.

## Download fatal motorcycle crash records
```{r}
#| label: group 4 download crash records

# motorcycles involved in crashes
g4_where_vehicles <- paste0(g4_where_dates, " AND (",
                            paste0("upper(vehicle_type) like '", g4_vehicle_patterns, "'", collapse = " OR "),
                            ")")
g4_vehicles <- read_portal_csv(
  soql_url(id_vehicles, `$where` = g4_where_vehicles, `$limit` = soql_limit),
  file.path(data_dir, "group04_vehicles_motorcycle_cache.csv")) %>%
  mutate(vehicle_class = if_else(str_detect(str_to_upper(vehicle_type), "MOPED"),
                                 "moped or motorized bicycle", "motorcycle"))

# crashes with at least one fatality, matched with the motorcycle crashes
g4_crashes_fatal <- read_portal_csv(
  soql_url(id_crashes, `$where` = paste(g4_where_dates, "AND injuries_fatal > 0"), `$limit` = soql_limit),
  file.path(data_dir, "group04_crashes_fatal_cache.csv")) %>%
  filter(crash_record_id %in% g4_vehicles$crash_record_id)

# people involved in the fatal motorcycle crashes
g4_people <- read_portal_ids(id_people, "crash_record_id", unique(g4_crashes_fatal$crash_record_id),
                             file.path(data_dir, "group04_people_cache.csv"))
```

## Fatal motorcycle crash points
People are summarized by crash: motorcyclists and others killed, and the age, sex, safety equipment (e.g., helmet use) and person type (driver or passenger) of the motorcyclist(s) killed.

```{r}
#| label: group 4 fatal motorcycle crash points

g4_moto_vehicles <- g4_vehicles %>%
  filter(crash_record_id %in% g4_crashes_fatal$crash_record_id)

# motorcycle types involved in each crash
g4_crash_vehicles <- g4_moto_vehicles %>%
  group_by(crash_record_id) %>%
  summarise(n_motorcycles = n(),
            motorcycle_type = paste(sort(unique(vehicle_type)), collapse = "; "),
            vehicle_class = if_else(any(vehicle_class == "motorcycle"), "motorcycle",
                                    "moped or motorized bicycle"),
            .groups = "drop")

g4_victims <- g4_people %>%
  mutate(age = as.numeric(age),
         age = if_else(age <= 0 | age > 110, NA_real_, age),
         killed = injury_classification == "FATAL",
         motorcyclist = !is.na(vehicle_id) & vehicle_id %in% g4_moto_vehicles$vehicle_id) %>%
  group_by(crash_record_id) %>%
  summarise(motorcyclists_killed = sum(killed & motorcyclist, na.rm = TRUE),
            others_killed = sum(killed & !motorcyclist, na.rm = TRUE),
            motorcyclist_killed_age = paste(na.omit(age[killed & motorcyclist]), collapse = "; "),
            motorcyclist_killed_sex = paste(na.omit(sex[killed & motorcyclist]), collapse = "; "),
            motorcyclist_killed_type = paste(na.omit(person_type[killed & motorcyclist]), collapse = "; "),
            motorcyclist_killed_safety = paste(na.omit(safety_equipment[killed & motorcyclist]), collapse = "; "),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("motorcyclist_killed_"), ~ na_if(.x, "")))

g4_crashes <- g4_crashes_fatal %>%
  select(crash_record_id, crash_date, posted_speed_limit, traffic_control_device,
         weather_condition, lighting_condition, first_crash_type, trafficway_type,
         roadway_surface_cond, intersection_related_i, hit_and_run_i,
         prim_contributory_cause, sec_contributory_cause, street_no, street_direction,
         street_name, num_units, injuries_total, injuries_fatal, latitude, longitude) %>%
  mutate(crash_date = ymd_hms(crash_date, tz = "America/Chicago", truncated = 3),
         crash_year = year(crash_date),
         crash_month = month(crash_date),
         crash_hour = hour(crash_date),
         crash_day_of_week = wday(crash_date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
         across(c(posted_speed_limit, num_units, injuries_total, injuries_fatal,
                  latitude, longitude), as.numeric),
         across(c(intersection_related_i, hit_and_run_i), ~ replace_na(.x, "N"))) %>%
  left_join(g4_crash_vehicles, by = "crash_record_id") %>%
  left_join(g4_victims, by = "crash_record_id") %>%
  mutate(across(c(motorcyclists_killed, others_killed), ~ replace_na(.x, 0L)),
         # if the people records have no fatality, use the crash-level count
         others_killed = if_else(motorcyclists_killed + others_killed == 0,
                                 as.integer(injuries_fatal), others_killed),
         total_killed = motorcyclists_killed + others_killed) %>%
  filter(crash_year %in% g4_years) %>%
  arrange(crash_date)

# crashes without usable coordinates (counted citywide but not mapped)
g4_crashes_unlocated <- g4_crashes %>%
  filter(is.na(latitude) | is.na(longitude) | latitude == 0 | longitude == 0)

motorcycle_fatal_crashes <- g4_crashes %>%
  anti_join(g4_crashes_unlocated, by = "crash_record_id") %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) %>%
  st_transform(3435)

# community area (nearest within g1_snap_ft, as for Group 1)
nearest_ca <- st_nearest_feature(motorcycle_fatal_crashes, community_areas)
nearest_ft <- as.numeric(st_distance(motorcycle_fatal_crashes, community_areas[nearest_ca, ], by_element = TRUE))

motorcycle_fatal_crashes <- motorcycle_fatal_crashes %>%
  mutate(comarea_id = if_else(nearest_ft <= g1_snap_ft,
                              community_areas$comarea_id[nearest_ca], NA_real_)) %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(community_areas) %>% select(comarea_id, comarea_name),
            by = "comarea_id")

rm(nearest_ca, nearest_ft, g4_moto_vehicles)
```

## Motorcycle fatalities citywide and by community area
```{r}
#| label: group 4 fatalities summaries

g4_count_cols <- c("fatal_crashes", "motorcyclists_killed", "others_killed", "total_killed")

fx_sum_fatalities <- function(crashes, ...) {
  crashes %>%
    group_by(...) %>%
    summarise(fatal_crashes = n(),
              motorcyclists_killed = sum(motorcyclists_killed),
              others_killed = sum(others_killed),
              total_killed = sum(total_killed),
              .groups = "drop")
}

# citywide by year (includes crashes without coordinates)
motorcycle_fatalities_city_year <- g4_crashes %>%
  fx_sum_fatalities(crash_year) %>%
  complete(crash_year = g4_years) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(g4_count_cols), ~ replace_na(.x, 0L)))

# by community area and year (zeros where no fatal crashes occurred), with rates
# per 100,000 residents
motorcycle_fatalities_ca_year_table <- motorcycle_fatal_crashes %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.na(comarea_id)) %>%
  fx_sum_fatalities(comarea_id, crash_year) %>%
  complete(comarea_id = community_areas$comarea_id, crash_year = g4_years) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(g4_count_cols), ~ replace_na(.x, 0L))) %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(community_areas), by = "comarea_id") %>%
  mutate(motorcyclists_killed_per_100k = round(motorcyclists_killed / population * 100000, 2)) %>%
  select(comarea_id, comarea_name, crash_year, all_of(g4_count_cols),
         motorcyclists_killed_per_100k, population) %>%
  arrange(comarea_id, crash_year)

motorcycle_fatalities_ca_year <- community_areas %>%
  select(comarea_id) %>%
  right_join(motorcycle_fatalities_ca_year_table, by = "comarea_id") %>%
  arrange(comarea_id, crash_year)

# one row per community area: motorcyclists killed by year and five-year totals
motorcycle_fatalities_ca <- community_areas %>%
  select(comarea_id, comarea_name, population) %>%
  left_join(motorcycle_fatalities_ca_year_table %>%
              select(comarea_id, crash_year, motorcyclists_killed) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = crash_year, values_from = motorcyclists_killed,
                          names_prefix = "motorcyclists_killed_"),
            by = "comarea_id") %>%
  left_join(motorcycle_fatalities_ca_year_table %>%
              group_by(comarea_id) %>%
              summarise(across(all_of(g4_count_cols), sum, .names = "{.col}_total")),
            by = "comarea_id") %>%
  mutate(motorcyclists_killed_total_per_100k = round(motorcyclists_killed_total / population * 100000, 2)) %>%
  arrange(comarea_id)
```
